key_insight: OpenThoughts-Agent introduces a fully open recipe for curating training data for agentic language models, aiming to make them generalize beyond a single benchmark. The key idea is that strong agents need diverse, purpose-built data pipelines—not just benchmark-specific datasets.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of publicly available guidance and reusable pipelines for training broadly capable agentic models. Existing open data efforts tend to optimize for one benchmark at a time, limiting cross-task generalization.
method: Build a fully open data curation pipeline for agentic model training.
Design data recipes intended to support diverse agentic behaviors rather than a single target benchmark.
Systematically explore how to construct training data for models that can generalize across varied agent tasks.
impact: This work gives researchers and practitioners a transparent starting point for creating stronger agentic models. It can help reduce reliance on opaque, benchmark-specific data recipes and improve reproducibility across agent evaluation and training.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing data collection, filtering, recipe design, and training.
Comparison chart of benchmark-specific datasets vs. the open general-purpose OT-Agent approach.

Flowchart illustrating how diverse training data improves generalization across tasks.
paper_title: OpenThoughts-Agent: Data Recipes for Agentic Models
paper_authors: Negin Raoof, Richard Zhuang, Marianna Nezhurina, Etash Guha, Atula Tejaswi
